site.title: Gordon Bailey — Internship Portfolio
site.lede: Everything built this summer, in one place. Six workstreams, from a peer benchmarking engine sellers can screen-share to the instrumentation and UTM plumbing underneath it. Each one keeps its own page with the same five headings: the problem, what was done, what came out of it, what it does not cover, and what the next person should pick up.

_comment: One node per page. `parent` nests it; `order` sorts within a parent.
status:  live      — real content, written and reviewed
drafting  — partial content on the page
awaiting  — page exists, content not yet supplied
`needs` is what has to be handed over before the page can be written. It
doubles as the card text while status is `awaiting`, so a blank page never
pretends to be a finished one.
`body` names a file in projects/ to inline as the page content. Omit it and
build.py renders the standard skeleton from `sections`.
sections: Who was stuck, on what, and why it mattered.
The actual work, in order, including what was tried and dropped.
Findings, decisions, shipped artifacts, numbers where there are numbers.
Scope held back deliberately, and the known soft spots.
The first thing the next person should do.

nodes.title: Hackathon
nodes.blurb: Sixteen hackathon projects, scored on one scale and tiered into build / validate / park — with an effort estimate from whoever wrote the code, and an honest read on which estimates do not exist yet.
nodes.h1: Which sixteen hackathon projects deserve a roadmap slot?
nodes.lede: A hackathon produces enthusiasm, not a roadmap. This scores all sixteen projects on GDV impact, churn prevention and feasibility, merges the duplicates, collects an estimate from each owner, and sorts them into four to build now, five to validate in Q3, and five to park with a named unlock.

nodes.title: Customer Intelligence
nodes.blurb: Three strands of the same question: how do we tell a customer something true about their own fundraising that they could not work out alone?

nodes.title: Fundraising Benchmarking
nodes.blurb: Groups every eligible nonprofit with organizations genuinely like it — same cause, same size — scores it inside that group, and turns the shortfall into a ranked list of levers. 3,161 accounts, 38 peer groups, 73% of variation explained.
nodes.h1: How is this organization really doing?
nodes.lede: Every nonprofit raises a different amount for different reasons. This compares each one against organizations genuinely like it — same cause, same size — and turns the difference into a short list of what to try next.

nodes.title: Competitive Intelligence
nodes.needs: Which competitors were in scope, where the data came from, and what the comparison was actually used for — pricing, positioning, or product gaps.

nodes.title: Customer Interview Synthesis
nodes.needs: How many interviews, how they were recruited, the coding scheme or themes you landed on, and the quotes you are willing to publish.

nodes.title: Instrumentation
nodes.needs: What was not being tracked, the event and property spec you wrote, what shipped versus what is still proposed, and how it gets validated.

nodes.title: UTM
nodes.needs: The tagging convention, what it replaced, who has to follow it, and how non-compliant links get caught.

nodes.title: Guides
nodes.blurb: Written so the next person does not have to reconstruct any of this from scratch.

nodes.title: Non-Functional Guide
nodes.needs: The guide itself, plus who the reader is — the requirements it covers, and the failure it is meant to prevent.

nodes.title: Data Architecture Repo Guide
nodes.needs: Which repo, how it is laid out, the path a change takes from branch to production, and the parts that bite newcomers.

nodes.title: Corporate Strategy
nodes.blurb: The growth argument the project work sits underneath.

nodes.title: How to Grow GDV
nodes.needs: The framing you settled on — which levers you argued GDV actually moves on, and the evidence behind each. The three questions below hang off it.
nodes.blurb: Three sub-questions, each with its own page.

nodes.title: How Do We Acquire Better Donors?
nodes.needs: What "better" means here — retention, gift size, referral, or lifetime value — and the acquisition sources you compared on it.

nodes.title: How Do We Build Better Relationships With Super Donors?
nodes.needs: Where the super-donor line sits, how many of them there are, and what is being proposed — product, service, or both.

nodes.title: How Do We Make Giving Cool?
nodes.needs: The audience you are aiming at, what currently makes giving feel uncool to them, and any concepts you tested.
